name: Durval

facts.text: Level 65, 30,000 health, crowd-control immune, armour factor 350 with 20% absorb; resists 20% of melee and 30% of everything else. His StartAttack is empty: he never melees.

He follows his target to spell range and casts in turn: Mesmerize (radius 450 around the target, range 1,500, 60 s, recast 40 s), Durval's Plague (120 s disease, recast 40 s), Shield of Bones (10 s bladeturn on himself, recast 10 s) and otherwise Smite (550 spirit, 3.5 s, uninterruptible, range 1,800, no recast).

Nine linked dead (PackageID DurvalBaf: five corpse delvers, four white lights) stand within about 500 of him. The script's call to them uses WorldMgr.GetNPCsFromRegion(3500), a region id, and finds nobody; they come by their own aggro (200, range 500) and faction bring-a-friend.
facts.source: source/server/GameServer/scripts/namedmobs/Albion Named Mobs/Shrouded Isles/Durval.cs; world data Mob.PackageID

facts.text: He walks home at full health when nobody is left on his aggro list; respawn is the epic-encounter interval.
Durval's order of the priests of the dead, the burial office he still says, the speaking priest who never lifts his hand, and the household he keeps are Living Server writing.

story:
Durval was a priest of the dead on Caldey before Morgana came, one of the order that kept the burying isle for the colleges of Avalon, and he took her coming as the answer to his prayers. The priests of the dead were not fighting men. Their office was words: the words said over a grave so that the dead lie down, the words said over a barrow so that it stays shut, and the words of the burying that send a soul on its way. Durval said them better than any priest on the isle, and for forty years he said them over the colleges' dead and wondered where they went. When the witch raised Caldey, the other priests said the words louder and were dragged down by the dead they had buried. Durval stopped saying them. He walked to his own barrow in the west of the isle and waited, and the dead let him be.

He has never lifted his hand against anyone since. He does not need to. He speaks. His smiting is the office of the burying said backwards, and it falls on whoever he looks at from farther off than an arrow flies; his sleep is the office for the watchers at a wake, which once let the mourners rest, and it falls on a little knot of people at once; and his plague is the sickness of the barrow, which keeps a wound from closing. When anyone comes at him with a blade he says a word and the bones of the barrow close round him like a shield, and the blow slides. He walks after those who try to get out of the sound of his voice. Nobody has.

He keeps a household. The corpse delvers who dig his barrow and the white lights that hover over it were the barrow's diggers and lamp-bearers in the colleges' day, and they stand close about him still, near enough that anything that comes for him comes into them first. The clan at Little Haven calls the barrow Durval's house and will not go into it short of a full company.

The Ledger of Little Haven has a page for him, blank. Mordwywr says the villagers will not let him write the priest's name in it until the priest is dead, because Durval buried most of their grandparents, and buried them well.
legend: Durval, level 65, 30k health, in his barrow in the west of Caldey. He never melees: he is a pure caster who follows you to range. His Smite is 550 spirit, 3.5 s, uninterruptible, range 1,800, and he chains it, so spirit resist and steady heals on whoever he is looking at. His mez hits everyone within 450 of the target for up to a minute (40 s recast), so the back line spreads and someone cures it. Cure his 2 minute plague. He bladeturns himself every 10 seconds, so open with something cheap. Nine of his household stand right on him, five corpse delvers and four white lights; the script's link is broken but they are close and aggressive, so expect them all and clear them first. He cannot be mezzed or stunned. A wipe resets him; respawn about an hour.

loremasterTopic.text: A priest of the dead of [caldey] who took Morgana's coming as the answer to his prayers. His office was words, and he still says them, wrongly: the burying backwards, the wake's sleep, the sickness of the barrow. He never lifts his hand. His delvers and white lights stand close about him in his barrow in the west.

bookPage: From the Ledger of Little Haven, kept by Mordwywr. Rose came to me and asked that I not write the priest's name on his page until he is dead. I asked why. She said he buried her grandmother, and her grandfather, and her mother's first child, and buried them well, and said the words better than anyone; and that when the witch called, every grave he had said the words over stood up with the rest, as if he had never said them. She said she would rather believe he meant them then. I have left the page blank. On the next page I wrote: a company of the clan went to the barrow and came back carrying five, all asleep.
